C45105.observed: What was checked: that each block of a job line on the printed page is separated from the next by a heavy line and a gap, so a mechanic has somewhere to write. What happened: the gap is there but the heavy line is not. Between one line's block and the next the page leaves a clear empty band about the height of three text rows, which is the writing space the requirement asks for. There is no rule drawn there at all - not a heavy one, not a light one. The measurement was taken on the printed page itself, on every row: the only heavy rule on the whole page is under the column headings at the very top, and the thin hairlines that do exist sit between the rows INSIDE a block, which is the opposite of what is wanted - the divisions within a block are drawn and the division between blocks is not. To be sure this was not a fault in how it was measured, the same measurement found the heading rule and eighty-three other ruled elements on the page, so it does see rules where there are any.
C45105.todo: What needs to be done: on the printed page, draw a heavy rule across the full width at the end of each job line's block, just above the blank writing band that already separates it from the next line. The writing band itself is correct and should stay as it is.

C45097.observed: What was checked: that a job with no customer on it prints the words 'No customer assigned'. What happened: this cannot be reached on this system, and it was tried properly rather than assumed. A job cannot be created without a customer - on the New Work Order window, leaving Customer empty and pressing Save answers 'Customer is a required field' and nothing is created. Every existing job on the system has a customer. So there is no job in the state this case describes, and the words it looks for can never be printed here.
C45097.todo: What needs to be done: this needs a ruling from the product owner. Either the product should allow a job to exist with no customer - in which case this case can then be run - or the requirement to print 'No customer assigned' does not apply to this product and the case should be retired. Nothing needs doing in the build until that is decided.

C45098.observed: What was checked: that a job with no vehicle on it prints the words 'No vehicle assigned'. The nearest real job, S2-6107, has a vehicle with only a year recorded and prints it as 'Vehicle: 1993' - that is thin information, not none. So there is no job in the state this case describes.
C45098.todo: What needs to be done: this needs a ruling from the product owner, the same one as the case about a job with no customer. Either a job should be allowed to exist with no vehicle, or the requirement to print 'No vehicle assigned' does not apply here and the case should be retired. Nothing needs doing in the build until that is decided.

C45104.observed: What was checked: that a job line marked Cancelled still prints, with its state shown. What happened: there is no Cancelled state for a job line in this product, so no line can be put into it. Opening a line and looking at its Status list on screen shows exactly four choices - Authorization required, Declined, Authorized and Complete - and the system refuses anything else. This was checked on the screen, not guessed from an error message.
C45104.todo: What needs to be done: this needs a ruling from the product owner on what the requirement means, since the product has no Cancelled state for a job line. Either a Cancelled state is meant to be added, or the requirement refers to something the product now calls by another name - most likely Declined - and the case should be reworded to that. Nothing needs doing in the build until that is decided.
